answers.reason: The faculty administrative officer holds a faculty-level administrative position without the rank required for the central university senate.
The faculty administrative officer is responsible for timetables, examinations, and records, not central budget allocation.
Selecting candidates for professorships is an academic matter outside the scope of the faculty administrative officer's duties.
As a faculty-level administrative employee without a high governance office, the officer is not automatically a member of the faculty council.
Because the officer organizes timetables and records for the faculty's degree programmes, their office falls within the scope of preparing changes to degree programmes.
The faculty administrative officer explicitly organizes examinations and records for the faculty, directly connecting their office to the examination board.
Awarding research grants is an academic matter unrelated to organizing examinations, timetables, and student records.
Because the officer manages records and timetables for degree programmes, they may take part in the lower-level working group revising module descriptions.
Choosing teaching laboratory equipment is outside the officer's remit of examinations, timetables, and records.
Because orientation week involves scheduling and introducing timetables and examination rules to new students, the officer's role permits participation in this lower-level planning round.
